item.description: NASA launched its Voyager 1 space probe in 1977. It's made it more than 16 billion miles in space, marking the farthest any human made object has ever traveled.

item.title: Walmart raises its outlook for the year for the 3rd time after a solid quarter
item.description: Walmart reported solid sales for the fiscal quarter as the discounter continues to attract a growing number of customers across the economic spectrum seeking to cut costs in the face of rising prices

item.title: WATCH: Man reunited with long-lost cat after 3.5 years
item.description: ABC News' Danny New talks to a woman in Oregon who helped reunite a missing cat with its owner in South Carolina.

item.title: Top U.N. court rules Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya
item.description: The International Court of Justice found that Myanmar security forces "acted with genocidal intent" against the Rohingya during the 2017 military operations in the northern Rakhine State.

item.title: Yahoo for the loo! An ode to the commode! Dotty for the potty! It's World Toilet Day!
item.description: November 19 marks the 25th anniversary of World Toilet Day. The theme this year: "Sanitation and Gender Equality: Safe Toilets, Equal Futures."

item.title: 'Grand Theft Auto VI', a 'masterpiece' 13 years in the making
item.description: PRESS REVIEW – Thursday, November 19: An historic trilateral summit takes place in Shenzhen between Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin. But is it more optics than substance? Also, a highly awaited decision from the International Court of Justice could redefine genocide. Finally, a huge cultural moment: "Grand Theft Auto VI" is out and the reviews are ecstatic.

item.title: Nigeria: States set to get their own police forces
item.description: Nigeria has moved a step closer to letting its 36 states set up their own police forces. The National Assembly has sent a constitutional amendment bill to the president, as authorities seek state-run police to complement the federal force amid growing insecurity. Many states currently fund vigilante groups to fight armed groups like Boko Haram, but these groups are poorly trained and ill-equipped for the task. FRANCE 24's correspondent has the latest.

item.title: French 2027 presidential race: Green leader Tondelier draws closer to hard-left Mélenchon
item.description: Six months before the first round of France’s presidential election, Green party leader Marine Tondelier is moving closer to Jean-Luc Mélenchon, the leader of the radical left. The move has caught the other candidates on the left and in the centre off guard, notably Raphaël Glucksmann. FRANCE 24's Clovis Casali explains.

item.title: Senegal: Pastef removes President Faye from its ranks
item.description: In Senegal, Pastef, the majority party led by National Assembly president Ousmane Sonko, has made official the departure of President Bassirou Diomaye Faye. It is the latest episode in a split with his former Prime minister that was already largely complete, and it comes in the middle of an economic crisis.

item.title: Crimean bridge attacked for 3rd time in a week, officials say
item.description: The Crimean bridge came under attack again overnight, according to Russian-aligned officials on the occupied peninsula, prompting the closure of the bridge to traffic.

item.title: Myanmar's Rohingya case: how does the ICJ define genocide?
item.description: The ICJ is preparing to rule on whether Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya, in a case brought by The Gambia after the 2017 crackdown. The key legal test is proving intent to destroy a group, which is notoriously hard, and the court’s reading of it could also weigh on South Africa’s case against Israel.

item.title: AI lab Anthropic sets stock market record with $81 billion IPO
item.description: Anthropic becomes the first "pure play" AI lab to go public, with an eye-watering $1.5 trillion valuation, a bellwether moment amid growing concerns of a financial bubble in the sector. Meanwhile, a scientific study shows US data centres are emitting as much greenhouse gas as entire nations.

item.title: 'We are making history,' says Trump at historic trilateral with Xi and Putin
item.description: The first meeting in history between US, Chinese and Russian leaders has kicked off in Shenzhen, China. "We are really making history," said the US president to his counterparts.

item.title: Judge extends temporary restraining order that blocks construction of Trump's arch
item.description: The original order was set to expire on Thursday.

item.title: APEC Summit: Lots of gloss, little real progress?
item.description: Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin are holding their first-ever trilateral meeting in Shenzhen, on the sidelines of the APEC forum. It is a historic moment in more ways than one, with the leaders of the world’s three most powerful countries around the same table. Ukraine, the war in Iran, nuclear disarmament and artificial intelligence are all expected to be discussed, and the summit has stoked fears of a carve-up of the world into spheres of influence. But despite the buzz, analysts expect more symbolism than substance, with few concrete breakthroughs likely. Our correspondent in the region has more.

item.title: Ukraine's European allies meet in Berlin in show of support
item.description: Ukraine’s main European allies are meeting in Berlin on Thursday as a show of support for Kyiv, with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner also attending. The gathering, which brings together the leaders of Germany, France, Britain, Poland and Italy as well as NATO chief Mark Rutte, takes place as Trump and Putin meet in China, fuelling fears in Europe that decisions on the war could be made without its input. FRANCE 24's correspondent in Germany has the latest.

item.title: Xi, Trump, Putin: historic summit ends, outcome unclear
item.description: The unprecedented trilateral summit between Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin ended on Thursday in Shenzhen after about an hour and 20 minutes. No details have emerged yet, but the three leaders talking face to face is already an event. Each has their own agenda: Putin wants to be back on the world stage, Trump needs a win at home, and Xi is asserting China’s status as an economic superpower. What comes out of it remains unclear, as FRANCE 24's journalists explain.

item.title: Gianni Infantino 'is not eligible' for FIFA presidency, Sepp Blatter says
item.description: In an interview with FRANCE 24, former FIFA president Joseph (Sepp) Blatter claimed that Gianni Infantino "is not eligible" to run in the upcoming election for FIFA president because he's running for the fourth time, which is forbidden "according to the existing statutes of FIFA". Blatter also accused Infantino of buying votes and of "using FIFA's money to go from one country to the other to decide them to sign for him".

item.title: WATCH: Trump's trilateral meeting with Xi and Putin begins
item.description: Presidents Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin began historic three-way talks to discuss Iran, trade and Russia’s war with Ukraine.

item.title: APEC Summit: Trump, Putin, Xi hold 'historic' meeting
item.description: 🇺🇸 🇨🇳 🇷🇺 US President Donald #Trump, Russia's Vladimir #Putin and Chinese leader #Xi Jinping kicked off their first trilateral talks in Shenzhen. Beijing said the meeting is aimed at "safeguarding world peace", but it has raised fears of a carve up of the globe into "spheres of influence".

item.title: Denmark ratifies Greenland security deal after months of pressure by Trump
item.description: Denmark's parliament on Thursday ratified a security deal involving Greenland and the United States. The vote comes months after the US, Denmark and Greenland ​signed the ‌agreement to end a standoff with the Trump administration over the Arctic island's future.

item.title: COVID was allowed to spread with 'deadly speed' and failure on borders was 'missed opportunity'
item.description: A lack of testing left the government "effectively blind" to COVID spreading across the UK, a report has found.

item.title: Infantino to face France's Diallo and Japan's Tashima in FIFA presidential election
item.description: FIFA confirmed on Thursday that France's Philippe Diallo and Japan's Kozo Tashima will run against incumbent Gianni Infantino in next year's presidential election. Infantino has faced criticism since July over his aborted plan to sell stakes in World Cup profits to private investors.

item.title: Two candidates to stand against Infantino in FIFA election
item.description: FIFA has confirmed which candidates will stand in next year's presidential election - as UEFA challenges restrictions placed on documents relating to the World Cup sell-off scandal.

item.title: France: Seven masculinists stand trial in Paris
item.description: Seven masculinists are facing trial in Paris on November 18 and 19. Aged between 26 and 54, the defendants are accused of sharing misogynistic, racist and anti-Semitic comments on a Telegram channel.

item.title: Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin begin unprecedented summit in China
item.description: Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin opened their first trilateral talks in Shenzhen on the sidelines of the APEC forum, a meeting analysts expect to offer more symbolism than breakthroughs and that critics fear could carve the world into spheres of influence. Ukraine, the Iran war, nuclear disarmament and AI are all expected to come up, while Trump and Xi also held one-on-one talks on trade and technology.

item.title: South Korea tightens security for national exam over AI cheating scandal
item.description: More than 550,000 candidates sat South Korea’s Suneung university entrance exam under extraordinary security, after an AI cheating scandal in which a top scorer on a national tax accountant exam admitted using a hidden mini camera to send questions to an AI system. Authorities inspected students’ glasses, deployed thousands of extra supervisors and ordered stickers over every button on candidates’ clothing. A nationwide disaster alert was also sent to make even muted phones buzz, exposing any devices smuggled into exam rooms.

item.title: Nuclear arms at the center of the Shenzhen trilateral meeting
item.description: Nuclear weapons are at the top of Donald Trump’s agenda at the trilateral summit in Beijing. The US president wants the United States, Russia and China to reduce their nuclear stockpiles, and FRANCE 24’s Philip Turle expects him to push hard for a three-way agreement on the issue. Iran is also a key part of the discussion. The three leaders share an interest in preventing the Iranian regime from acquiring nuclear weapons. Regional conflicts and oil prices are also se to be central issues.

item.title: Skyscraper in Riyadh damaged as Saudi Arabia reports surge in new Houthi attacks
item.description: A skyscraper in Saudi Arabia's capital Riyadh was damaged on Thursday after the Gulf country reported new attacks by Yemen's Houthis. Witnesses said the city's Public Investment Fund Tower, which showcases Saudi Arabia's economic ambitions, was "damaged across several floors, with windows blown out".
